newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chechen aide arrives in Moscow for talks.
newsitem.headline: Chechen aide arrives in Moscow for talks.

text.p: An aide to Chechnya's separatist leader Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev arrived in Moscow on Friday for talks with Russian officials on a draft agreement intended to clarify relations between Russia and the breakaway region.

Akhmed Zakayev, who is a security adviser to the Chechen rebel chief, is expected to meet members of Russia's powerful Security Council, including its secretary Ivan Rybkin, over the weekend, Itar-Tass news agency reported.

The talks will focus on a range of political and economic issues expected to feature in the accord, which will govern relations between Moscow and Chechnya in the period up to January 27, when elections will be held in the region.
Rybkin has said Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, keen to become more involved in resolving the vexed Chechen issue, could go to the Caucasus for the signing of the agreement.

Chechnya, an oil-rich land on the southern edge of the Russian Federation, was devastated in 21 months of fighting between Chechen rebels and Russian troops sent there in December 1994 to crush the region's independence.
Tens of thousands of people, mainly civilians, died in the fighting which ended with a peace deal struck by Moscow with the rebels on August 31.

Moscow, bent on persuading the region's rebel leaders to remain within the Russian Federation, has proposed making Chechnya a free economic zone, a move which would excuse the region from tax and duties.
